review.summary: Reviewed the handshake, record update and application stream paths for signature and crypto issues. The TLS-to-record binding is checked on both dial and accept, and record updates are verified and bound to the same endpoint and instance. One hypothesis remains: a record's own expiry is not re-checked on an open connection, so identity claims can outlive the signature that granted them.

findings.title: Identity claims on an open connection are not re-checked against record expiry
findings.prerequisites: A peer endpoint E holds a valid record R that lists identity X and expires at time T. E keeps its QUIC connection open past T and sends no newer record. The record's identity owner stops re-signing for E, so R is never renewed. This is a hypothesis: whether the expiry bound is meant to revoke authority on live connections is not documented in the supplied files.
findings.impact: After R expires, handle_app_stream still accepts streams whose from is X on that connection, and find_connection still routes requests for X to it. The signature that authorised X on E is no longer valid under the record's own expiry rule, but nothing re-checks it on the live connection. Only membership expiry is swept (membership_loop), not record expiry.
findings.evidence: handle_app_stream: "} else if !peer.contains(&header.from) {" where peer = c.peer(). register stores the verified record and never reads expires_at: "let (peer_tx, peer_rx) = watch::channel(peer.clone());". membership_loop sweeps only check_member(&peer), and find_connection filters only on is_closed, contains, seq and is_superseded. control_reader accepts an update only when VerifiedRecord::verify succeeds and new.seq() > current.seq().
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the record's expires_at with the connection (for example in ConnInner, or read it from peer.expires_at()). Check it in find_connection and in handle_app_stream, and have membership_loop, or a similar sweep, close connections whose peer record has expired, with a dedicated close code. Add a test that a connection whose peer record has expired stops accepting streams claiming that peer's identities.
findings.validation_needed: Confirm in record.rs that expires_at is exposed and that VerifiedRecord::verify does not re-check expiry at use time. Then write a test: establish a connection with a short-lived record, advance time past expiry without a new update, and check that open_bi and handle_app_stream still accept identity X.

limitations: record.rs, membership.rs and the signer are not supplied, so the checks VerifiedRecord::verify performs (expiry, signature coverage, trailing bytes, the sequence number rule) are taken from the review brief rather than read from source.
Whether records are meant to bind identities only until expiry on live connections is not stated in the supplied docs; the finding depends on that.
No test files were included in the three supplied files, so existing test coverage of these paths is unknown.
Key generation, storage and file permissions for a fixed iroh secret key are not visible in these files (Builder::secret_key takes an in-memory key only).
The membership certificate is not covered by the record signature (a known limit) and was not re-examined.
